avalancheActivity.comment: In the highest elevations of the High Tatras, the Western Tatras, and the highest elevations of the western part of the Low Tatras, a low avalanche danger—Level 1—persists above the 1,800-meter elevation. This is primarily due to wind-drifted snow on the leeward slopes (east and southeast) of the highest elevations. Be cautious of very steep areas, narrow gullies, and notches where snow accumulates. Here, due to precipitation combined with strong winds, small snow slabs and pillows may form on leeward slopes. Light snowfall and strong winds are still expected throughout the day, especially in the morning.
avalancheActivity.highlights: Watch out for drifted snow on the leeward sides (E, SE).

snowpackStructure.comment: After the passage of a cold front, a cold air mass has moved into the mountainous regions of Slovakia. On Sunday, the weather will be influenced by an area of high pressure. We expect clear to partly cloudy and cold weather. The snow line is at 1,500 meters above sea level. Due to low temperatures, the snow remains powdery and, at the highest elevations, lies on top of an old, hard snowpack. These two layers are not sufficiently bonded and form a dangerous layer prone to detachment—especially under additional weight. The thickness of the new snow layer may vary depending on the aspect, but averages 20–30 cm.
